proof.criterion: RootHears leaves main's resume behaviour as it was, and a parked root's held start task is sent by its next start, never lost
proof.surface: The same whole daemon (TestTesterRootHearsMainPathsLive), counting the prompt frames the architect's shim receives

A re-admission: prompted its start task naming ask-p once. A fresh admission: architect spawned, 0 prompts, as main starts a first admission with no task. A parked root: its re-admission start queued the task naming ask-h and forgot the decision; parked before the architect came up, the architect then registered and was held (0 prompts, 1 pending, 0 kept); on the next re-admission (a start with no task of its own) the held task was prompted once.

Returning true leaves the drive green: on the whole daemon the park also suspends the architect claim, which holds the task by itself, so RootHears' own effect (a claim live while its root is parked) is proven only by the property test's seeds and the supervise unit tests.

propertyModelGaps: Spec decisions arrive only through the ask path: the outbox's parkDecision on an undelivered design-approved/changes-requested notice is not driven, nor RelayNotParked (a lingering root moved back to a running status) or a session's decision. Covered on the whole daemon by the round-7 drive.

The readmitted_approvals pair is never kept: readmit does not run admission's keepStaleApproval, so the Approved/Latest half of KeptDecisions and its claim, hand-over and forget are untested by the property test.

The fake runtime never fails a launch or resume: no claim failed, RequestRetry, launch budget, retired claim, or the notice executor's 'architect will not hold its role again' branch. Covered on the whole daemon by the stale-start and round-7 drives' refused resumes.

No linger expiry or tree close (linger_close, ClearTreeGeneration, a child carried into a tree of its own), no children (a child's decision naming its root), no awaiting_person root or ResumeAwaitedRoot task (the other phase-less run task RootHears holds), no operator delivery or operator suspend.
Publish answers modelled: delivers, no-holder, refused, receipt-timeout; not modelled: publish denied, delivery_failed retries, an unroutable notice, a re-hold budget spent.

Single-threaded and the clock never moves: no two lanes or two daemons running rows of the root at once, no lease expiry, backoff, re-hold delay or linger deadline. The model reimplements admission's start enqueue rather than calling admit.Admission, so the two can drift.
notes: Latency, not a failure: on the whole daemon the hand-over's catch-up waited 23 s after the stale start released the decision before it was published; the hand-over commit wakes no lane, so the row waits for the outbox's next poll.

In my harness the hand-over catch-up carried gate policy "" where the ready's catch-up carries root-issues: the outbox takes cfg.Gates.Design raw, the engine defaults "" to root-issues, and the test config leaves gates unset. Production config always sets the gate (config defaults root-issues), so this is a harness artifact.
